fields.h1: Build Tax Automation That Chases the Paperwork
fields.hero_description: Build tax automation that collects client documents and W-9s, chases what is missing, and tracks every return by status.
fields.features_heading: What a Tax Season Runs On
fields.features_subheading: Tax automation sends the requests and reminders around each return. Emergent builds it from a prompt; preparers keep the judgment.
fields.feature_1:
Checklists drawn from last year's return

Each client gets a list of the forms their prior-year return used, with one upload link. The list updates as files arrive, and the preparer sees every missing form by name.
fields.feature_2:
AI reads the form type on every upload

An AI step reads each uploaded file into fields such as the form type, tax year, and payer. Any field the AI is unsure of goes to a person on your team to confirm first.
fields.feature_3:
W-9s on file before the first payment

The app requests a W-9 when a contractor is added and keeps it with that contractor's payment records, ready for Form 1099-NEC reporting. The app itself files nothing.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders by email, Slack, or in the app

Pick the day a reminder goes to a client and the day a late item moves to a partner. Each reminder names the missing item and links to it, with no tax figures or account numbers.
fields.feature_5:
Connects to the tools your practice runs

The app connects to any tax, accounting, or document tool with an API, such as QuickBooks or Xero. Client and return records sync in and out, so nobody types a name twice.
fields.feature_6:
Your tax app's code, in your GitHub

Export the app's full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Client records stay in a database you own, and your IT lead can review exactly who is able to open them.

fields.hero_prompt: Build tax automation for my 140-client firm that emails each client a document checklist and tracks every return by status.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up tax automation?

plan.angle: The top 10 are enterprise tax software vendors (Thomson Reuters, RSM, Avalara), a few tax-prep AI products, a Reddit thread and a webinar, all selling a product or talking about the future of the profession. None shows the paperwork around a return moving on its own. This page shows four jobs a tax practice or a small business runs every season, each with its trigger, its rule and its record: a document checklist built from last year's return, W-9s collected before a contractor's first payment, engagement letters signed before prep starts, and a board of returns by status against the firm's own cutoff. The app organizes the work and the records; it gives no tax advice, calculates no tax and files nothing.
tab_stories: Hollisbrook Tax Group sends client Marisol Penrice a checklist built from last year's return with a W-2, two 1099-INT forms and a Form 1098; the app reads each upload's form type and tax year, 3 of 4 are in, and the 1098 still missing after 7 days sends her an email reminder.

Ottaway Joinery pays 12 contractors and has 11 W-9s on file; new drafter Ysolde Rautio gets a W-9 request when she is added, and her $650.00 invoice stays out of the Friday payment run until her W-9 arrives.

Soderqvist Tax Partners sends 86 engagement letters for e-signature, 79 are signed, a return's prep task opens only after its letter is signed, and a letter unsigned after 10 days goes to partner Halvard Nyquist by Slack direct message.

Tollgate Row Tax tracks 140 returns on one board: 52 ready to file, 18 in review, 61 in prep and 9 waiting on documents, and 21 days before the firm's March 31 cutoff the 9 waiting returns go to partner Faustina Strachan as one list.
